item.title: Our predictions for URI, Providence, Brown and Bryant women's hoops
item.description: Last season was 30 years in the making for the women's basketball programs in the state. The University of Rhode Island finally authored a breakthrough on behalf of Brown, Bryant and Providence. There was a local favorite to cheer in the NCAA Tournament at long last, as the Rams put together a dream campaign in the Atlantic 10. URI's subsequent loss to Alabama in the Round of 64 was a last game in charge for coach Tammi Reiss , who was hired away to battle the Crimson Tide directly with an SEC rival at Florida. Colleen Mullen takes over for a leader in Kingston who was singular in nature to date in that program's history – the lone conference tournament champion, the all-time leader in victories and win percentage, the builder who tripled average attendance at the Ryan Center from her first day on the job through her last. That afternoon in Louisville closed the 2025-26 chapter of the women's story in the state – the next chronicling 2026-27 will be opened Monday night . The Bears, Bulldogs and Friars will all have eyes on matching and exceeding what the Rams achieved last year while building toward their own dream appearances in March Madness. Who could have a realistic chance of making some history through the next six months? Let's take a look at one main question facing each program. Can URI sustain success this time? Mullen committed as a player to the Rams in the wake of a 21-8 season and their lone previous NCAA Tournament bid in 1996. URI didn't win double-digit games again until 2000-01 and couldn't top the .500 mark until 2002-03. It's been a difficult challenge for the Rams to produce anything lasting over their modern history. Sophia Vital returning is a good start, a preseason all-conference selection and dynamic guard at both ends of the floor. Having her perform like one of the league's best would allow a mostly new roster to settle into their respective roles a bit more comfortably. Vital is the only member of the Rams who scored a single point with the team in 2025-26 – Amori Jarrett was a redshirt who didn't appear in a game. Mullen brought four players with her from Albany, and their ability to adjust against superior competition in the Atlantic 10 will be key. Delanie Hill and Anais Levasseur should both earn backcourt minutes, while Amaya Stewart and Martina Borrellas should be fixtures in the paint. URI has made a concerted effort during its summer workouts and preseason practices to blend the former Great Danes with those who either stayed with the Rams or arrived from elsewhere. Narragansett native Mia Fiore (Merrimack) and former Moses Brown standout Lauren Bousquet should both have a place in the rotation alongside Wofford transfer Queen Ikhiuwu. item.title: Milwaukee Bucks broadcasts are free this season as the team rebuilds
item.description: The Milwaukee Bucks see their decision to show all games on television for free this season as an investment in the fans. The Bucks will broadcast all 82 regular season games on MY24 and statewide affiliates in partnership with Rincon Broadcasting Group. The move comes after a disappointing season and the decision to trade superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo “You all get free games every night here and that’s a pretty good deal, and we reach a lot more people,” Bucks co-owner and governor Wes Edens said at the team media day. “It was the right decision to make from ownership and from the business side of it.” Fans can also watch on YouTube TV and with most cable packages. The change comes after the team's former TV carrier, Main Street Sports, which oversaw the FanDuel Sports Wisconsin network, closed its regional-sports network operation. It's the first time in more than 30 years that Bucks broadcasts will be available over the air at no cost. It was a “substantial economic decision,” Bucks president Josh Glessing said in an interview with the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel. “I won’t get into the exact dollar amount (lost). The structure is very different than it historically would have been in terms of being on a RSN and collecting your rights fee,” Glessing said. “We’re in the ad business now.” The Bucks aren’t the only team struggling to find a local broadcasting partner as more money shifts to larger national broadcasting outlets. “That’s something the league is very focused on addressing, as are we,” Edens said. The Bucks aren’t the only ones in Milwaukee that have been impacted by shrinking local TV deals. The Milwaukee Brewers have also been impacted financially. In March, Brewers principal owner Mark Attanasio said bringing the broadcast in house was “about a $20 million surprise.” “It's a pretty big one-off. item.title: ‘I love your tight end’: Donald Trump praises Travis Kelce after mocking Taylor Swift for years
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect President Donald Trump hasn’t exactly had the warmest relationship with Travis Kelce and Taylor Swift over the years. But on Sunday night, Trump went out of his way to show the Kansas City Chiefs tight end some love. Speaking at a rally in Kansas shortly after the Chiefs’ loss to the Denver Broncos, Trump told the crowd that he loves their tight end. It was a surprising change of tone, considering how he has talked about Kelce’s wife, Taylor Swift. Trump, Kelce, and Swift Trump and Swift have a long adversarial relationship going back to the 2016 election, when Swift openly opposed Trump, endorsing Hilary Clinton instead. That cold relationship has continued into recent years. Back in 2023, Trump predicted that Kelce and Swift’s relationship wouldn’t last. He said he hoped they enjoyed their life, “ maybe together, maybe not — most likely not .” Ahead of the 2024 election, Trump tried to win Swift’s endorsement anyway. In a Truth Social post, he wrote, “I like her boyfriend, Travis, even though he may be a Liberal, and probably can’t stand me!” When Swift endorsed Kamala Harris instead, and Trump responded on Truth Social by writing, “I HATE TAYLOR SWIFT.” Ahead of Super Bowl LIX in February 2025, Kelce said it would be a “great honor” to have Trump at the game. But after Swift was booed in the stadium, Trump mocked her on Truth Social, writing that “MAGA is very unforgiving!” That reportedly didn’t sit well with Kelce . And when Kelce and Swift got married in July, the White House mocked Swift on social media . Swift has since quietly had her music muted from White House and Team Trump TikTok videos. ‘I Love Your Tight End’ The Chiefs blew a 24-13 fourth-quarter lead in Denver on Sunday, falling 28-24 to drop to 5-2. Trump addressed the loss at his rally later that night. “And I did not want to interfere with your football game, but maybe I should have because that ending was— now I’m a big fan of your coach and your quarterback, and I love your tight end. I think it’s good. They’ll be fine,” Trump said, in a clip shared by Rapid Response 47 . “But that was a nasty ending, wasn’t it? Looked like they had it. Mahomes is so good. And I figured, boy, oh, boy, can’t come closer. But that was quite a game,” he continued. While it was obviously a disappointing end to the game, Trump made it clear that he thinks the Chiefs are “But you’ll be fine. You have a great team,” Trump said. item.title: Ravens QB Tyler Huntley could miss TNF vs. Jags with suspected turf toe
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Tyler Huntley #5 of the Baltimore Ravens throws the ball as he's getting tackled during the first half against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens are evaluating backup quarterback Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley for a suspected turf toe injury, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. An MRI on Monday will shed further light on his status for Thursday night’s matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Huntley, 28, entered Sunday’s game against the Buffalo Bills after starter Lamar Jackson injured his throwing hand on the first snap of the game. He faced constant pressure and was hit multiple times before leaving the game in the second quarter. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finished the game under center while taking several shots of his own, though he “hopes” to be ready to play on Thursday. Jackson is set to land on injured reserve to undergo surgery on his right thumb, which will sideline him for at least four games. Huntley would be in line to start in his place, as he did in Jackson’s three-game absence following a Week 4 high ankle sprain. However, confirmation of his initial turf toe diagnosis will almost certainly keep him from playing in Week 9 – and potentially longer. Instead, it will likely be Fagnano making an unlikely first start of his NFL career vs. the Jaguars, who boast an elite run defense but have struggled against opposing passers this year. The former UConn starter could only complete 10 of his 21 passing attempts for 91 yards and an interception on Sunday afternoon, good for a paltry 4.3 yards per attempt and a 40.0 quarterback rating. Getting reps with Baltimore’s first-team offense will give him a chance at a better showing against Jacksonville, but Fagnano will clearly be facing an uphill battle. Huntley largely struggled in his five appearances this year. His numbers through the air are at or above league-average, but his underpowered arm limited the Ravens’ downfield passing game. He was not helped by a leaky, banged-up offense line that slowed the run game and far too often allowed rushers right in his lap. Turf toe injuries can linger, especially for a quarterback whose game is built on his mobility. Huntley could miss not only Thursday night’s game, but more contests after that, potentially positioning Fagnano for multiple starts. The Ravens will already need to add quarterback depth just to get through the week, but a longer-term absence from Huntley could force them to make a more substantial move.

item.title: Cleveland Browns news: What the hell was that?
item.description: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another year, another disastrous road trip to Pittsburgh for the Cleveland Browns. Cleveland played its annual game against the Steelers in Pittsburgh on Sunday and lost for the 23rd consecutive time. That ties the NFL record for most consecutive regular-season road losses against one team in NFL history, as the Browns now join the Detroit Lions, who lost 23 consecutive road games to the Green Bay Packers from 1992 to 2014. It is fitting that the Lions are involved, as Detroit and Cleveland are the last two NFL teams to go 0-16 in a season. item.title: Michael Strahan raises Aaron Donald retirement question as Rams comeback falters
item.description: Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images Michael Strahan has questioned whether Aaron Donald could be having second thoughts about returning to the NFL after the Los Angeles Rams legend endured a difficult start to his comeback. Donald came out of retirement after nearly two years away from football, with expectations high that the three-time Defensive Player of the Year could transform the Rams’ defence. However, injury problems have limited his impact. The Rams have now improved to 4-4 after beating the Los Angeles Chargers 24-9, but questions remain over Donald’s fitness and how much he can contribute following his return. Michael Strahan wonders whether Aaron Donald regrets Los Angeles Rams comeback Speaking on the Roommates Show, Strahan admitted he was surprised when Donald initially retired and questioned whether the defensive tackle might be reconsidering his decision. “I love Aaron. Aaron’s another good buddy of mine. He’s a great player. I was surprised he retired in the first place. He had years left in him,” Strahan said. The former New York Giants star then pointed to Donald’s early struggles, including missing the Rams’ opening game and dealing with a back issue after facing the Denver Broncos. “I’m pretty sure after that first game, when he didn’t even travel, but they got beat, and then he played last week with a back issue. So I’m wondering if they’re the point where he’s going, ‘damn, why’d I come back?’” Donald has made it clear that individual statistics are not his priority. The defensive tackle said his focus is on helping the Rams win rather than adding to his already impressive collection of accolades. “I didn’t come back to try to earn individual accolades or anything. I did that, accomplished that. It doesn’t excite me. The only thing that excites me is winning,” Donald said. The 35-year-old has recorded 111 career sacks, earned 10 Pro Bowl selections and eight first-team All-Pro honours, while playing a key role in the Rams’ Super Bowl LVI triumph. His return was expected to give Los Angeles a major defensive boost, but injuries have disrupted those plans. Donald also had an awkward moment against the Chargers when he failed to secure a loose ball that could have given the Rams an excellent scoring opportunity. Head coach Sean McVay joked that he would give Donald a hard time over the mistake, but the Rams will need their veteran defender to stay healthy as they look to build momentum. After moving to 4-4, Los Angeles has an opportunity to improve its position. Donald’s fitness and ability to make a consistent impact will remain important factors in that push. item.title: No. 7 Cougars turn attention to rivalry game after hardfought win over Arizona State
item.description: BYU Cougars quarterback Bear Bachmeier (47) is shoved back by a group of Arizona State defenders during a game at LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News BYU coaches and players had a lot to unpack after bouncing back from that difficult loss at UCF with a 27-20 win over Arizona State on Saturday afternoon. Tackling issues, costly turnovers and more uneven play on special teams kept the Cougars from turning in the type of dominating performance they were looking for in front of 63,332 at LaVell Edwards Stadium. But an ugly win is better than a pretty loss, and it didn’t take BYU long to start thinking about this week’s game, where the only thing that matters is the final score. “Just an away game, and, yeah, we are just gonna keep the same process and play our game.” BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier on facing No. 3 Utah Of course, we are talking about the long-awaited showdown with the Utes, who remained undefeated (8-0) with an easy 49-25 win at Cincinnati and soared to No. 3 in the Associated Press Top 25 poll released on Sunday. BYU (4-1, 7-1) jumped to No. 7, meaning that Saturday’s 10 a.m. rivalry game at Rice-Eccles Stadium will be the first-ever BYU-Utah matchup pitting top-10 teams. BYU head coach Kalani Sitake knew the Utes had won when he spoke to reporters after the Cougars held off ASU, but was not aware of how dominating the performance was. Utah led 42-6 at halftime and coasted in the second half. “That (rivalry game) is different every time,” said Sitake, who owns a three-game winning streak in the rivalry. “No matter what you guys think is going to happen, it is a different (game). I am more focused on trying to get our team (playing better).” A definite priority for the Cougars this week will be improving their rushing attack, after they picked up only 47 yards against an ASU defense that had been allowing around 146 per game. Meanwhile, in Cincinnati, Utah had 268 rushing yards as quarterback Devon Dampier and running backs Daniel Bray and Wayshawn Parker had big days. BYU played without reigning Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year LJ Martin the last four games, and will definitely need the senior to contribute if it hopes to pull off an upset and win for the second-straight time in Salt Lake City. item.title: Carlos Alcaraz closes in on Roger Federer’s all-time record after winning the Vienna Open title
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz has already enjoyed a career that most could only dream of, and is only just getting started. The Spaniard, in record-breaking time, has amassed seven Grand Slam titles and a further eight Masters 1000 triumphs. Roger Federer , Rafael Nadal and Novak Djokovic did things few thought were possible across their illustrious careers, but even their legacies feel under threat. Whether they care about their records staying intact or not remains to be seen, but if they are, they’ll be worried about the rate at which this 23-year-old sensation is racking up wins. Other than Jannik Sinner, it really feels like there is nobody who can challenge him when he is at full fitness. His latest title in Vienna only adds further proof to this suggestion, as another Nadal record has been equalled, with a Federer record not far behind. Carlos Alcaraz closes in on Roger Federer feat and equals Rafael Nadal record The first record Carlos Alcaraz has managed is matching his fellow Spaniard, moving up to eight different ATP 500 events won. They lead Juan Martin del Potro, Andy Murray and Boris Becker on seven, and Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic on six. And, whilst the second record has yet to fall, it feels inevitable that it will sometime in 2027. After all, there are only two players who have won 25 consecutive matches at ATP 500 tournaments: Alcaraz and Federer. The Swiss superstar saw his run halted at 28 wins, with Alcaraz just two away from matching that, having won his last 26. Photo by Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto via Getty Images This extends back to April 2025, having actually not lost a single match in events at this level throughout 2026. The only one he entered and did not win was the Barcelona Open, where he was forced to withdraw due to injury. Alcaraz beat Alex de Minaur to win the Vienna Open yesterday, marking his first-ever title at this event. He now heads to Paris hoping to maintain that form and potentially even win another first-time trophy, and put himself in the perfect position to thrive at the ATP Finals.

item.title: 5 takeaways from the Steelers’ 27-6 win over the Cleveland Browns
item.description: Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images | Getty Images In a Week 8 battle for the AFC North lead, the Steelers let their play do the talking in a dominant win over the rival Cleveland Browns in Pittsburgh on Sunday. As always, there are plenty of takeaways to be had: 1. Some things never change It’s been a year of change in the AFC North as three teams have new head coaches. Pittsburgh is no longer under the long-time leadership of Mike Tomlin, while the Browns, with Todd Monken replacing Kevin Stefanski, shocked the world by leading the division through seven weeks. But the Browns haven’t won a regular season game in Pittsburgh since 2003, and all that offseason turnover didn’t do anything to change that. History continued. Emphatically. The Steelers won 27-6 in their most lopsided victory yet this season. The Browns were repeatedly punched in the mouth in a game that never felt particularly close. Much in the way that it’s easy to dismiss what happens in a Steelers’ Thursday Night Football loss in Cleveland — in what feels more like an annually-scheduled night of disappointment rather than a football game with free will — I believe it’s a bit of an overreaction to suddenly declare the Steelers as Super Bowl contenders in a win as clearly telegraphed as this one was. But at the same time, the story of the game is less about the win and more about how the Steelers won. The pass rush was masterful. The run game was relentless. Pittsburgh’s roster seemed to relish every moment of punishing its rival. The team culture seems to be in a great place, and the Steelers have their most established identity of the season on both sides of the ball after the big win. When the Steelers hired Mike McCarthy, it was clearly in part a decision to try to keep a similar status quo from the Mike Tomlin era. Yes, plenty has changed in terms of scheme and other details, but the macro-level results: an above-average team, rebounding from brutal losses such as the Patriots in Week 2, and of course, routinely defeating the Browns at home, remains the same. 2. The Steelers dominate the trenches Eight sacks. Fourteen quarterback hits. Nonstop pressure. The Steelers’ pass rush was absurdly good Sunday afternoon, defeating the Browns’ offensive front with speed and power and making Cleveland quarterback Deshaun Watson distribute the ball from a war zone. What was even more impressive for Pittsburgh was how the production was spread across the board, with seven different defenders recording 0.5 sacks or more. The box score doesn’t do it justice, either. Outside linebacker Alex Highsmith was arguably the team’s MVP against Cleveland, logging just a 0.5 sack but generating six pressures against Browns left tackle Spencer Fano, including two quick pressures. item.title: A look back at the memories – and emotions – from Cubs 2016 World Series run
item.description: Cubs fans celebrate after game seven of the 2016 World Series against the Cleveland Indians outside of Wrigley Field. Cubs won 8-7. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-USA TODAY Sports Ten years ago today, I wrote the words I had been preparing my whole life for: The Chicago Cubs have won the World Series. The Cubs are champions. Let that soak in. For a long while. The 108-year drought is over. The moment millions upon millions of people dreamed about for their entire lives is here. It’s actually here. This is not a dream. You are not asleep. That was exactly what I penned for what was then known as CSN Chicago. I will say one thing, however — it certainly felt like a dream at the time. Even as I wrote those words, it felt surreal. And 10 years later, it still doesn’t quite feel real. I was born into Cubs fandom. My parents, sisters, uncles, aunts, cousins and friends were all diehard Cubs fans. Growing up in the Chicagoland area, I was always drawn to baseball — and always drawn to the Cubs and their historic championship drought. I was also drawn to writing. As a kid, I created my own Cubs team on loose-leaf paper and went through a whole season, detailing each lineup and game of my pretend team. Through high school, it started to become clear that I had a way to merge my two passions — writing and baseball (namely, the Cubs). And thus my singular professional goal was born — to be in the Cubs clubhouse when they won it all, documenting the historic moment. In some ways, it was a potentially tragic goal. I didn’t have any control over how the Cubs performed on the field or how the front office put together the roster. But I turned it into a career, working for what was then called CSN Chicago (which later became NBC Sports Chicago). I grew into a role as the backup on the Cubs beat, working with Patrick Mooney to provide coverage as Theo Epstein and Jed Hoyer built the team that eventually won it all. In the years leading up to 2016, I had opportunities to move in my career — to change cities and take other jobs. But that was going to take me away from my goal, so I passed on all of those gigs. I stayed in Chicago and eventually had the chance to travel to cover the Cubs in places like Milwaukee, St. Louis, Los Angeles … … and Cleveland. item.title: Eagles suffer ugly NFC East loss vs. Commanders: Who’s to blame?
item.description: LANDOVER, Md. — The Philadelphia Eagles ’ losing streak extended to six games on Sunday night, losing to the Washington Commanders, 27-10, at Northwest Stadium. The Eagles (2-6) are in last place in the NFC East after another ugly loss. And with the trade deadline approaching, it’s time to start thinking of this team as a seller. Here’s who’s to blame for the Eagles’ latest embarrassing loss in primetime. OC Sean Mannion: Once again, the Eagles did not score in the third quarter. They’re averaging 1.6 points per game in the third quarter, worst in the league. The Eagles completely wasted a two-for-one opportunity at the end of the first half (poor play-calling by Mannion) and to start the third quarter. Mannion had a couple of creative calls (the Saquon Barkley-Wildcat touchdown, Dallas Goedert’s QB sneak). But it just wasn’t enough to wash away an ugly offensive performance. OL coach Chris Kuper: At some point, the constant unblocked pressure against the blitz not only falls on the players, but also the coach. Kuper was tasked with replacing arguably the best offensive line coach in the NFL in Jeff Stoutland. And the offensive line has looked like a complete mess this year, no matter who’s in there. Whether it’s miscommunications or assignments, Kuper has to do better. OT Markel Bell: The rookie right tackle had been playing well the last few weeks . But this game was one to forget. Bell was pushed back into Tanner McKee on a consequential strip sack. And then, when the Eagles lined up to go for it on fourth-and-4 at Washington’s 13-yard line in the fourth quarter, Bell jumped offside. That forced a field goal attempt, which, after another penalty, Jake Elliott doinked. QB Tanner McKee: The strip sack was also on McKee. He has to feel the pocket better. He has to have better awareness. McKee battled out there, getting hit like crazy. But McKee just isn’t a good enough backup option. That much is clear. EDGE Jonathan Greenard: Greenard helped Jalen Carter clean up a sack. But that was about it. His effort against the run, in particular, was pretty poor. Not what the Eagles want to see from the former Pro Bowler that they traded two third-round picks for and gave a $100 million contract. HC Nick Sirianni: Sirianni always preaches the details and mastering the things “that require no talent.” Well, this team is not detail-oriented. It hasn’t been all season, and it wasn’t on Sunday night for all to see. Sirianni isn’t the one out there committing the penalties and mental errors. item.title: No Starc, Cummins or Hazlewood in squad as Australia name several new faces for England series
item.description: Australia have named several new faces in their white-ball squads for the upcoming series against England, with young fast bowler Mahli Beardman and allrounders Jack Edwards and Liam Scott among those receiving call-ups. Batting prospects Ollie Peake and Jake Fraser-McGurk have also been included, along with wicketkeepers Lachlan Shaw and Sam Harper. Mitchell Marsh will captain both the ODI and T20I teams. "These ODI and T20 matches provide several players, many of whom have had opportunities on recent tours, with a great chance to further demonstrate their ability against very strong opposition," said chairman of selectors George Bailey. Beardman, Peake, Edwards, Scott, Nikhil Chaudhary and Joel Davies have made their white-ball debuts in recent times. Shaw and Harper are the only uncapped players in the squads. "They are good examples of players who have had an opportunity at the international level and have continued working on their game from what they learnt from those experiences," added Bailey. Australia will play three ODIs against England at home from November 13 to 18, followed by a five-match T20I series. The matches will give the next generation of Australian players an opportunity to make a case for selection ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup, which will be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. With a home Test series against New Zealand coming up, fast bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood have been rested from the white-ball squads. The trio featured in Australia's 2-1 Test series defeat in South Africa. Travis Head, Alex Carey, Matt Renshaw, Josh Inglis, Cooper Connolly and Cameron Green have been named in the ODI squad but will not feature in the T20Is. After the New Zealand series, Australia will travel to India for a five-Test series. That will be followed by a 150th anniversary Test against England in Melbourne and an Ashes campaign. "We are in the middle of a highly demanding phase of our schedule," said Bailey, referring to Australia's Test players. "To manage this workload, each player's build-up to the New Zealand series will be carefully planned and focussed on individual's physical and mental preparation." 135451606

Toronto has maybe bigger issues to address, but you can never have enough starting pitching, especially in the AL East,” Roche wrote. The Blue Jays are going to need a healthy rotation, and King could help provide the stability they are looking for. He is coming off a solid campaign with the Padres and would give Toronto another experienced option at the top of its rotation. King made $25 million with San Diego before opting out of his contract.
